body.statement: The interval \(I_{T,\Delta}\) is \(O_{T,\Delta}\)-measurable and uniformly honest over \(\mathfrak M_T(\alpha,\beta,L,c,C,\varepsilon)\cup\mathfrak M_T^{\mathrm{low}}(\alpha,\beta,L,c,\varepsilon)\) without conditioning on \(E_T\) and without convergence of \(t^\alpha\pi_t(1)\). Measurability follows from the recorded calendar revelation times: main-prefix and old-prefix age-window indicators are known at \(H_T\), including when a response remains unrevealed. On \(\mathfrak M_{T,\Delta}^{\mathrm{reg}}(\kappa)\), \(\sup_x|P\{(\widehat\tau_{T,\Delta}-\tau+b_{T,\Delta})/\widehat s_{T,\Delta}\leq x\}-\Phi(x)|\to0\) and \(\widehat s_{T,\Delta}/s_{T,\Delta}\to1\) uniformly. If the gate fails, \(I_{T,\Delta}^{\mathrm{conc}}\) retains coverage; if it passes, \(I_{T,\Delta}^{\mathrm G}\) has the bounded-shift Gaussian coverage envelope, including triangular arrays with variance approaching the threshold \(1/\log T\).
body.justification: This is the load-bearing uniform studentization result that makes one implementable procedure valid in both Gaussian and degenerate regimes.
body.gap: Bibaut et al., Hadad et al., and Shi, Wang, and Wu rely on centered scores plus variance consistency or convergence; none treats an outcome-selected reveal process with an overlapping correction and an observable low-variance splice.
body.consumer: The theorem yields a prespecifiable implementation that does not fail when the inferior-arm outcome variance is small or the adaptive allocation oscillates.
